subject: RE: Novamed - DPA redlines and MSA tieouts
messages:
From: Elise Brunet <elise.brunet@novamed.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pierre Martin <pierre.martin@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:14:00 +0200
Subject: Novamed - initial DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are Novamed's consolidated redlines to the DPA (PDF) and a short spreadsheet that maps each redline to the MSA/Order Form clause we think needs alignment. High-level items:

- Novamed is proposing a carveout for model training (Section 2.3) — they want explicit controller/processor language where customer data will not be used to improve vendor models.
- Expanded sub-processor disclosure cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) — they ask for a faster notification window.
- SCCs: they want the EU SCCs (2021) applied plus an addendum for specific hosting territories; we flagged Azure Germany as preferred.
- Roles: disagreement on controller/processor split for analytics derived from tokens retained in logs.

Can you confirm the expected internal review timeline and who from Redwood legal/engineering we should expect feedback from? Our procurement also needs a run-from-complete-redlines deadline to lock the Q3 procurement window.

Attachments: Novamed_DPA_redlines_2027-07-28.pdf (redline), Redline_summary_table.xlsx (mapping)

Best,
Elise
Legal Counsel | Novamed
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Brunet <elise.brunet@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 14:03:00 +0200
Subject: RE: Novamed - initial DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Hi Elise — thanks for sending these over and for the summary. I downloaded the PDF and spreadsheet. Quick reply with how we'll structure the review:

1) Legal redline pass (Laura) — we will produce a comment-by-comment response and a clean copy for signature. Target 4 business days (EOD Mon 2 Aug).
2) Engineering ops / KMS + hosting (Ben) — Ben will confirm whether Azure Germany meets our hosting and export controls constraints and whether we can offer an explicit training carveout.
3) Procurement / commercial run-through (me) — I'll confirm timelines on the Order Form changes and any pricing impact from hosting or SLA changes.

A few asks for Novamed to help speed this: can you call out the top 6 must-haves in the spreadsheet (we saw 12 items) and identify which ones are deal-terminating vs. preferred? Also, flag any internal approvals you need (e.g., security committee) and target dates.

I'll loop back with a consolidated reply and proposed language. If we need an exceptions path for the training carveout, we'll propose limited language with compensating safeguards (audit rights + dedicated KMS).

Sofia
Senior Legal Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novamed - initial DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Sofia / Laura — quick tech ops notes after reviewing the redlines:

- Azure Germany (DE) is supported in our Private offering; hosted API currently doesn't have tenancy in that region. We can route customer traffic to DE if they take a Private deployment or a Dedicated pool pinned to DE.
- Training carveout: we can offer a contractual commitment that customer data will not be used to train our public models if they choose Dedicated or Private, provided they accept a 12% surcharge (to cover model isolation + KMS usage).
- Sub-processor cadence: monthly disclosures are operationally feasible but will require a small process change; we can commit to a monthly report for critical sub-processors (security, storage, infra) and quarterly for others.

I'll draft short technical text and a one-paragraph SOW addendum describing the Dedicated/Private routing and KMS commitment.

Ben
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Elise Brunet <elise.brunet@novamed.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pierre Martin <pierre.martin@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:37:00 +0200
Subject: RE: Novamed - initial DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Thanks — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from Novamed procurement and security:

- The training carveout is a must-have for us unless Redwood will guarantee a technical separation and wipe policy that is independently auditable. Can you confirm what "model isolation" means operationally and whether we can include an audit right tied to SOC 2 scope?
- The surcharge is OK but procurement needs an estimate in USD and whether that number is one-time or recurring.

We've flagged three redlines as deal blockers in the spreadsheet (rows 2, 5, 9). We can be flexible on the sub-processor cadence if Redwood will commit to the monthly report for critical subs.

If you can provide a draft amendment that includes the Dedicated/Private option language, audit scope, and a ballpark surcharge by EOD Mon 2 Aug, we can route for internal sign-off and keep to our Q3 procurement window.

Regards,
Elise
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Brunet <elise.brunet@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 17:05:00 +0200
Subject: RE: Novamed - initial DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Elise — agreed on timeline. Summary of action items we will deliver by EOD Mon 2 Aug:

- Legal clean redline + comment matrix (Laura) — addresses controller/processor language and proposed SCCs wording.
- Ops/technical amendment (Ben) — describes Dedicated/Private deployment routing to Azure DE, technical definition of "model isolation" (KV cache purge, no retained training artifacts), and proposed audit window tied to SOC 2 plus evidence sharing cadence.
- Commercial estimate (Sofia) — ballpark surcharge in USD and whether recurring vs. one-time.

We will mark the three Novamed rows you flagged as "deal blockers" and provide alternative language where feasible. If anything changes on your end, please update the spreadsheet link (I have editing rights).

I'll upload the drafts to the Drive link and share a DocuSign envelope if Novamed wants to sign the amendment once agreed. Proposed next step: 30-minute call Tue 3 Aug to walk the amendment if your team can.

Sofia
